title: 👓 Korea Proposes a Law: AI Glasses Must Announce When They Are Recording!
body: 👓 Korea Proposes a Law: AI Glasses Must Announce When They Are Recording!
A lawmaker in the South Korean parliament has introduced a bill requiring AI glasses to tell people around them that they are recording, to protect people's privacy in public places.

The bill includes two amendments: the first requires manufacturers and importers to install a recording-alert feature in wearable recording devices such as smart glasses, with technical measures to prevent disabling it, and bans making or selling tools designed to turn it off.
The second amendment requires anyone recording with smart glasses or a smartwatch to inform the people they are filming, whether by light or by sound, whatever the purpose of the recording.

The proposal came after an incident in July, when police investigated a man who secretly filmed a date with smart glasses after hiding the recording indicator, then posted the video on social media. The data protection authority also warned on 9 November that smart glasses look like ordinary glasses, making it hard for people around you to notice you are recording, and that the alert can be easily disabled.
Current law does not require manufacturers to add an alert feature, and the duty to inform is limited to recording in workplaces only, not to private recordings between individuals.
Simply put: Korea wants you to always know when smart glasses are recording you... so do you feel safe with these glasses spreading around you?
Have you ever suspected someone was filming you with their glasses without you knowing?
